item.title: 1983: Cal Ripken Jr. Named AL MVP, Edging Teammate Eddie Murray
item.description: Cal Ripken Jr. of the world-champion Baltimore Orioles is selected named American League MVP, edging teammate Eddie Murray. Ripken gets 15 first-place votes and 322 points, while Murray garners 290 points and ten first-place nods. Carlton Fisk gets the remaining three top-of-the-ballot votes. Photo: Joe Shlabotnik (CC BY 2.0).

item.title: 2023: MLB Owners Approve Athletics Relocation to Las Vegas
item.description: Last day for article xx (B) free agents to accept a qualifying offer from a former club (midnight EST). MLB owners approve of Oakland Athletics relocation to Las Vegas. Photo: SVeach94 (CC BY-SA 4.0).

item.title: 2021: Kevin Cash Named AL Manager of the Year for Second Straight Year
item.description: Kevin Cash of the Tampa Bay Rays was named American League manager of the year for the 2nd straight year while Gabe Kapler of the San Francisco Giants was named National League manager of the year. Photo: Arturo Pardavila III from Hoboken, NJ, USA (CC BY 2.0).

item.title: 2019: Kilkenny Wins New York Hurling Classic at Citi Field
item.description: On November 16, 2019, Citi Field hosted the New York Hurling Classic—a one-day hurling tournament featuring Limerick, Kilkenny, Tipperary, and Wexford for the Players Champions Cup—which was won by Kilkenny. Photo: Ajay Suresh from New York, NY, USA (CC BY 2.0).

item.title: 2018: Derek Jeter Unveils New Miami Marlins Logo and Uniforms
item.description: Miami Marlins CEO Derek Jeter unveiled a new logo, team colors and uniform for the 2019 MLB season. The new design replaced the one used after the club moved to Marlins Park in 2012, and switched from the Florida Marlins to the Miami Marlins.

item.title: 2012: Royals Sign Wood to Minor League Contract
item.description: On November 16, 2012, the Kansas City Royals confirmed they had signed Wood to a minor league contract. Photo: L-Rey on Picasa Web Albums (Original version) UCinternational (Crop) (CC BY 3.0).

item.title: 2011: Cubs Offer Sveum Vacant Managerial Position
item.description: On November 16, 2011 the Chicago Cubs offered Sveum their vacant managerial position. Photo: thotfulspot (CC BY 2.0).

item.title: 2010: Marlins Trade Dan Uggla to Braves for Dunn and Infante
item.description: The Florida Marlins trade Dan Uggla to the Atlanta Braves for Michael Dunn and Omar Infante. Photo: User ScottRAnselmo on en.wikipedia (CC BY-SA 3.0).

item.title: 2010: Oakland Proposes Jack London Square Site for New A's Ballpark
item.description: On November 16, 2010, the City of Oakland proposed a waterfront site in the Jack London Square area for a new A's ballpark.

item.title: 2009: Bailey Named 2009 AL Rookie of the Year
item.description: 876 WHIP, Bailey was named 2009 American League Rookie of the Year on November 16, 2009. Photo: Keith Allison on Flickr (CC BY-SA 2.0).

item.title: 2007: Barry Bonds Indicted on Perjury and Obstruction Charges
item.description: Barry Bonds is indicted on charges of perjury and obstructing justice. Photo: Jim Accordino at https://www.flickr.com/photos/jimmyack205/ (CC BY 2.0).

item.title: 2000: Jeff Kent Named National League MVP for Giants
item.description: Jeff Kent of the San Francisco Giants was named the National League MVP. Photo: Ryosuke Yagi (CC BY 2.0).

item.title: 1996: Charlie Neal, 65, Three-Time All-Star and Gold Glove Second Baseman
item.description: Charlie Neal, 65, three-time All-Star and Gold Glove Award winner at second base, who appeared in 970 career games with the Brooklyn/Los Angeles Dodgers, New York Mets and Cincinnati Reds from 1956 through 1963; hit .370 for the Dodgers in their 1959 World Series victory over the Chicago White Sox, and drove in the first Met run in their inaugural season of 1962. Photo: Unknown author (Public domain).

item.title: 1992: Rockies Sign Andrés Galarraga, Reunite With Don Baylor
item.description: The Colorado Rockies sign free agent first baseman Andrés Galarraga, who rejoins Don Baylor, his hitting coach with the St. Louis Cardinals. Galarraga is coming off his second injury-plagued year, having missed 44 days of the season after being hit on the wrist by a Wally Whitehurst pitch in the third game of the season. Photo: User Dlz28 on en.wikipedia (Public domain).

item.title: 1989: Giants Sign Former NL All-Star Kevin Bass
item.description: The Giants sign outfielder Kevin Bass, a former NL All-Star, granted free agency from the Houston Astros three days ago.

item.title: 1988: José Canseco Unanimous AL MVP, Winning All 28 First-Place Votes
item.description: José Canseco is the unanimous choice as the American League Most Valuable Player, winning all 28 first-place votes cast. Canseco led the AL in homers (42), RBI (124) and slugging (.569), and also stole 40 bases in 1988. He becomes the Junior Circuit's first consensus MVP since another Oakland outfielder, Reggie Jackson, in 1973.

item.title: 1981: Cubs Sign Harry Caray Away From White Sox for WGN-TV
item.description: The Chicago Cubs steal a crucial free agent from their South Side rivals, when the parent Tribune Company's WGN-TV signs Harry Caray as their play-by-play broadcaster away from the White Sox. Already a legend over his 37-year career, which began as the voice of the Cubs' NL arch-rivals, the St. Louis Cardinals, Caray, now 67, has been the star of the White Sox' radio/TV booth since 1971. Photo: Photographer-Ed Meyer, St. Louis Globe-Democrat. The newspaper ceased (Public domain).

item.title: 1979: Anaheim Stadium Hosts American Final Speedway Qualifier
item.description: On November 16, 1979, Anaheim Stadium hosted motorcycle speedway, when it was the venue for the American Final, a qualifying round for the 1980 edition of the Speedway World Championship.

item.title: 1978: Dave Parker Wins 1978 NL MVP With 21 of 24 First-Place Votes
item.description: Future Baseball Hall of Fame inductee and Pittsburgh Pirates right-fielder Dave Parker, already a Gold Glove recipient, now wins the 1978 National League Most Valuable Player Award with 21 of 24 first-place votes.

item.title: 1977: Rod Carew Beats Cowens and Singleton to Win AL MVP
item.description: Rod Carew of the Minnesota Twins easily beats Al Cowens of the Kansas City Royals and Ken Singleton of the Baltimore Orioles to win the 1977 American League MVP Award.

item.title: 1966: Roberto Clemente Named NL MVP, First Puerto Rican to Win
item.description: Roberto Clemente of the Pittsburgh Pirates (202 hits, 29 HR, 119 RBI, and a Gold Glove right fielder in 1966) is selected the Most Valuable Player of the National League by the BBWAA. The future Hall-of-Famer is the first Puerto Rican and second Latin American to capture an MLB MVP award. Photo: Unknown author (Public domain).

item.title: 1962: Perini Sells Milwaukee Braves to Bartholomay Syndicate for $5.5 Million
item.description: Principal owner Louis R. Perini sells the Milwaukee Braves to a syndicate headed by Chicago businessman William Bartholomay for a reported $5.5 million. Perini originally bought into the Braves in 1944, when they were based in his home city of Boston, then moved them to Milwaukee in 1953. Photo: Unknown author (Public domain).

item.title: 1955: Comiskey, Rigney to Share White Sox Baseball Operations Duties
item.description: Chicago White Sox owner Grace Reidy Comiskey announces that her son, Chuck Comiskey, who turns 30 in three days, and son-in-law Johnny Rigney, 41, an ex-ChiSox pitcher, both vice presidents, will share baseball-operations duties formerly performed by Frank Lane, who quit as general manager two months earlier.

item.title: 1954: Ralph Kiner Traded to Indians as Player to Be Named Later
item.description: Future Hall-of-Fame slugger Ralph Kiner becomes a "player to be named later" in an earlier (September 30) transaction when the Chicago Cubs ship him to the Cleveland Indians as part-payment for pitcher Sam "Toothpick" Jones. The trade will conclude on November 30 when the Cubs receive outfielder Gale Wade (also a "PTBNL") and $60,000 from Cleveland.

item.title: 1945: Jake Northrop, Former Boston Braves Pitcher, 1918-1919
item.description: Jake Northrop, pitcher for the Boston Braves from 1918 to 1919.

item.title: 1914: Plank Jumps From Athletics to Federal League Chicago Federals
item.description: Eddie Plank reportedly jumps from the Philadelphia Athletics of the American League to the Federal League's Chicago Federals after Athletics owner Connie Mack instigates a fire sale, asking waivers for Plank, Jack Coombs, and Chief Bender. Photo: Paul Thompson (Public domain).

item.title: 1907: Baseball Film How Brown Saw the Baseball Game Hits Theatres
item.description: The baseball film How Brown Saw the Baseball Game is released in theatres. Photo: The Billboard (Public domain).

item.title: 1887: Rules Committee Drops 4-Strike Rule, Returns to Three Strikes
item.description: The joint rules committee drops the 4-strike experiment from 1887 and returns to the standard 3-strike rule. The committee also drops the base on balls as counting for a hit in official statistics.

item.title: 1886: Joint Committee Sets 5 Balls for Walk, 4 Strikes for Out
item.description: The joint rules committee between the National League and the American Association announce the new rules for the 1887 season which include 5 balls for a walk, 4 strikes for an out, the batter calling for pitch location being abolished and establishing a strike zone between the knees and shoulders of the batter. Photo: Strauss (Public domain).
